finding: Under `git.base-branch: auto`, land refuses only `main` and `master`. In a repository whose default branch has another name (for example `trunk`, set as the remote's HEAD) and that the forge does not protect, land pushes the fix straight onto the repository's base branch.
why: The module docstring makes it a refusal: ship.py:24-26 "Refused when Base is the repository's base branch (`auto` reads as main and master): a fix for it ships through open, never land." CONFIG.md:92-93 defines `auto` with more fallbacks: "`git.base-branch: auto` resolves to `origin/main`, else `origin/master`, else the branch's upstream, else `HEAD`." The repository already reads the remote's default branch for the same guard: scripts/protected-lookup.py:155 `names = {"main", "master", default_branch(common, remote)} - {""}`.
fix: Under `auto`, refuse `main`, `master` and the remote's default branch read from `refs/remotes/<remote>/HEAD` (the `default_branch` read in scripts/protected-lookup.py:144). Refuse when that ref is unset and neither `main` nor `master` exists on the remote. Change the docstring at ship.py:25 to match, and add a test with a remote whose HEAD is not main or master.
evidence: ship.py:606 `    if target in ({"main", "master"} if base == "auto" else _base_names(cwd, base)):`. Probe <scratch>/ds0007r3/test_probe_ds.py::test_auto_trunk_repo_lands_onto_its_base: remote with HEAD -> trunk and no main, config `schema: 1` (so `_base_branch` returns `auto`), Base `trunk@<tip>`, protected=() -> `{'step': 'land', 'status': 'done', 'push': 'trunk@8f8cff322a4b8b9b60678e7b9f8ffeba72094d06', 'how': 'pushed'}` and the remote trunk moved to the fix commit (2 passed). || also (logic-correctness, medium): Under `auto`, land refuses only `main` and `master`, but CONFIG.md resolves `auto` past them to the branch's upstream. In a repository with no origin/main and no origin/master (default branch `develop`, no git block in the config), a diagnosis with Base `develop@<sha>` lands straight onto develop. Probe (scratch pytest on the test_ship fixtures, real `_base_branch`, protected lookup false, diagnosis branch tracking origin/develop): `_base_branch` answered `auto`, the CONFIG.md chain gives `origin/develop`, and land answered `{'status': 'done', 'push': 'develop@00adf76...', 'how': 'pushed'}`.

finding: Land now needs the Base commit, but the parse finds it only when hex digits come directly after `@` or whitespace. No format file defines that shape. A Base written as `feat/export (<commit>)` or `feat/export at <commit>` gives an empty commit, and every land of that diagnosis is refused. Inferred, not verified: diagnose can write such a shape, because its instructions name no separator.
why: skills/utils/diagnose/DIAGNOSIS-FORMAT.md:16 `| Base | the branch the reproduction started from, and its commit id | no | no | diagnose |` defines no grammar for the cell. skills/utils/diagnose/SKILL.md:35 says only "Record the Base branch and the commit the worktree starts from." check_diagnosis.py and diagnosis_file.py have no check on the Base shape (no match for `base` in either file). The only `{branch}@{commit id}` grammar is the `push` entry (DIAGNOSIS-FORMAT.md:58).
fix: Give the Base row the `{branch}@{commit id}` grammar in DIAGNOSIS-FORMAT.md (its owner) and refuse other shapes in check_diagnosis.py. Until then, name the expected `{branch}@{commit id}` shape in the `_carries_a_fix` refusal reason at ship.py:632.
evidence: ship.py:283-284 `    base, *rest = re.split(r"[@\s]+", first("base").replace("`", "").strip(), maxsplit=1)` / `    commit = re.match(r"[0-9a-fA-F]{4,40}\b", rest[0]) if rest else None`. Probe <scratch>/ds0007r3/test_probe_ds.py::test_base_written_with_parenthesised_commit_refuses_land: Base `feat/export (<real commit>)` -> base_commit '' and `{'step': 'land', 'status': 'refused', 'reason': 'the diagnosis Base names no commit, so land cannot tell whether fix/bug-export-drops-row carries a fix commit'}`. || also (logic-correctness, medium): The Base commit is found only when it follows the branch name directly after `@` or whitespace. The format gives Base no grammar, so a diagnosis that writes the commit in another shape now has every land refused. Probe: Base `` `feat/export` at `9f2c1ab` ``, `feat/export (9f2c1ab)` and `feat/export — 9f2c1ab` all parse to `base_commit == ''`. A land with Base `feat/export at <real sha>` and a real fix commit answered `refused`: "the diagnosis Base names no commit". Before this delta the same diagnosis landed, because only the branch name was read.

finding: The no-fix guard only checks that HEAD is not at or behind the Base commit. A diagnosis branch moved to the feature's newer tip with no fix commit (a pull or reset before the fix was committed) passes the guard. The read-first then finds the remote tip equal to HEAD, so land reports a push that shipped nothing. Probe: Base `feat/export@<start>`, a stranger pushes one commit onto feat/export, the diagnosis branch is reset to it. Land answered `{'status': 'done', 'push': 'feat/export@e81e810...', 'how': 'found'}` and listed `push: feat/export@e81e810...`.
why: round 2 finding r-005 (scratchpad r2-0007-merged.json), which this guard closes: "Accept the contained-in answer only for a HEAD that carries a fix commit."; ship.py:629 "Refuse a land whose HEAD is the Base commit or behind it: no fix commit to push."
fix: Require at least one commit in `{base_commit}..HEAD` that the Diagnosis branch made itself. For example, check that the branch reflog (`git reflog show --format=%H %gs {branch}`) has a `commit` entry for one of those commits, and refuse otherwise. Add a test in which the diagnosis branch is reset to a moved feature tip and land is expected to answer `refused`.
